newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Strangles traded in Cable & Wireless.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Strangles traded in Cable & Wireless.

text.p: Traded options in telecommunications group Cable & Wireless attracted a lot of interest on Monday as a number of traders took positions in the options, dealers said.
By mid-afternoon, the biggest deal was the sale of 2,000 July 500 puts at 24p as well as 2,000 July 550 calls at about 19p in a short strangle strategy.

If the position is held to expiry it will make a maximum profit of 43p if the underlying stock is anywhere between 500p and 550p. In a separate deal, another trader bought 750 July 500/550 strangles at the same prices.
At July expiry, the long strangles will make money if C & W shares either go below 457p or above 593p.
There was also a crossed trade of 250 lots, with the same options series and at the same option premiums.
By 1510 GMT, Cable & Wireless shares added 6p to 512p.
A short straddle was the main deal in electricals group GEC, in which 450 May 390 puts were sold at 10p as well as 450 May 390 calls at about 18p.
The underlying shares fell 2-1/2p to 392p but for the short straddles to make a maximum profit of 28p, GEC shares need to be 390p at expiry.
Over in index options, activity was restrained despite the stock market's plunge and the main deals were volatility trades.

One such deal was the purchase of 250 March 4400 calls at 20-1/2p in the FTSE 100 index options against selling March FTSE futures at 4405. In general, the deal will make money if stock market volatility increases because option premiums go up with volatility.
At 1510 GMT, spot FTSE was down 45.3 at 4379.0 while March futures were down 26 at 4378.
